significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that standard reaction transformers encode donor/acceptor and bond-electron structure, use it causally in product generation, and exhibit a predictive coupling whereby “electron-flow representation strength predicts where the model generalizes vs hallucinates”; taken together, this includes a form-(iii) law rather than merely an existence probe or single steering result. It would constrain architectural and auditing decisions beyond the probed representation—particularly whether direct predictors such as Molecular Transformer should be augmented or replaced by explicitly mechanistic approaches such as ELECTRO or FlowER—and would explain both product changes and a family of OOD/error outcomes. The claim establishes both a phenomenon and a mechanism, while the operational negative branch (“no more decodable than shuffled controls” and no selective intervention effect) distinctly supports the recipe-learning account, although it would not rule out every possible nonlinear encoding. Under the topic-substitution check, the generic topic would only suggest probing whether scientific mechanisms are represented; it would not supply this causal-plus-predictive electron-flow conclusion, so the score is driven by the claim-specific increment.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the claimed per-reaction “electron-flow strength” predictor and the recovered “electron-source or bond-breaking directions”; the former could gate or audit a generated reaction before it is trusted in synthesis planning, giving practical lead time before laboratory use even though it is computed around prediction time. After per-model re-extraction, the intervention directions themselves merely provide a new place to look, but the asserted relation—weak or inconsistent electron-flow representation predicts hallucination and OOD failure—still predicts a qualitative result in another standard product-prediction transformer. The hypothesis covers the Molecular Transformer/Chemformer class trained on reactant-to-product SMILES, and its downstream users include model auditors and synthesis-planning practitioners, though it does not assert transfer to arbitrary architectures or scientific domains. Removing these specific handles and retaining only the assigned topic would not justify this reach score, so the topic-substitution check passes.
